# .github/workflows/deploy.yml
# build -> test -> deploy (canary region first) -> canary analysis -> slack on failure
name: build-and-deploy

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main, 'release/**' ]
    tags: ['v*.*.*']
    paths-ignore:
    - 'docs/**'
    - '**.md'
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      environment:
        description: Where to deploy. Prod requires an approved change ticket in the change-management channel, no exceptions after the October incident.
        type: choice
        options: [staging, prod]
        default: staging
      dry_run:
        description: "Render manifests + diff only"
        type: boolean
        default: false
      regions:
        description: 'Comma separated, e.g. "us-east-1,eu-west-1" (empty = all)'
        required: false
        default: ''
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 3 * * 1-5'   # nightly staging redeploy to catch drift
  merge_group: {}

permissions:
  contents: read
  packages: write
  id-token: write    # OIDC -> AWS
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  group: deploy-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}  #only cancel stale PR runs

env:
  REGISTRY: ghcr.io
  IMAGE_NAME: ${{ github.repository_owner }}/kestrel-gateway
  DEPLOY_ENV: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' && 'prod' || 'staging' }}
  TARGET_ENV: ${{ (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.environment) || (startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v') && 'prod') || 'staging' }}
  HELM_VERSION: "3.15.2"
  KUBECTL_VERSION: v1.30.2
  PYTHON_VERSION: "3.10"
  FORCE_COLOR: "1"

jobs:
  lint-test:
    name: Lint & test (py ${{ matrix.python }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
    timeout-minutes: 20
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        python: ["3.10", "3.11", '3.12']
        include:
          - python: "3.12"
            experimental: true
    services:
      redis:
        image: redis:7.2
        ports: ["6379:6379"]
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "redis-cli ping"
          --health-interval 5s
          --health-timeout 3s
          --health-retries 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      -   name: Set up Python
          uses: actions/setup-python@v5
          with:
            python-version: ${{ matrix.python }}
            cache: pip
      - name: Install
        run: pip install -r requirements-dev.txt && pip install -e ./services/flags-sync -e ./tools/rollout
      - name: Lint
        run: |
          ruff check . --output-format=github
          yamllint -c .yamllint.yml deploy/ .github/   # strict: warnings fail the build
          # schema check against the published supergraph
          npx --yes @graphql-inspector/cli diff "git:origin/main:schema/supergraph.graphql" "schema/supergraph.graphql" --rule suppressRemovalOfDeprecatedField
      - name: Test
        run: pytest -q -n auto --maxfail=5 --cov=services --cov-report=xml:coverage.xml -m "not slow and not gpu" --junitxml=reports/junit-${{ matrix.python }}.xml
        continue-on-error: ${{ matrix.experimental == true }}
        env:
          REDIS_URL: redis://localhost:6379/0
          FLAGD_OFFLINE_FLAG_SOURCE_PATH: ./flags/flags.test.yaml
          TZ: UTC

  build:
      needs: lint-test
      if: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' || !github.event.pull_request.draft }}
      runs-on: [self-hosted, linux, x64, docker]
      outputs:
          image_tag: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.version }}
          digest: ${{ steps.push.outputs.digest }}
      steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with: {fetch-depth: 0}
          - uses: docker/setup-qemu-action@v3
          - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
          - name: Log in to GHCR
            uses: docker/login-action@v3
            with:
                registry: ${{ env.REGISTRY }}
                username: ${{ github.actor }}
                password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          - id: meta
            uses: docker/metadata-action@v5
            with:
                images: ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}
                tags: |
                    type=ref,event=branch
                    type=semver,pattern={{version}}
                    type=sha,format=short,prefix=
          - id: push
            uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
            with:
                context: .
                file: services/gateway/Dockerfile
                platforms: linux/amd64,linux/arm64
                push: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' }}
                tags: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}
                cache-from: type=gha
                cache-to: type=gha,mode=max
                build-args: |
                    GIT_SHA=${{ github.sha }}
                    BUILD_DATE=${{ github.event.head_commit.timestamp }}

  deploy:
    needs: [build]
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
    environment:
      name: ${{ env.TARGET_ENV }}
      url: https://${{ env.TARGET_ENV == 'prod' && 'api' || 'api.staging' }}.kestrel.dev/graphql
    strategy:
      max-parallel: 1
      fail-fast: true
      matrix:
        # fmt: table
        include:
          - {region: us-east-1, cluster: prod-use1-blue, canary: true, weight: 5}
          - {region: eu-west-1,  cluster: prod-euw1-blue,canary: false,  weight: 100}
          - {region: ap-southeast-2, cluster: prod-apse2-a, canary: false, weight: 100}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Configure AWS credentials (OIDC)
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
        with:
          role-to-assume: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/gha-deploy-${{ env.TARGET_ENV }}
          aws-region: ${{ matrix.region }}
          role-duration-seconds: 3600
      - name: Install helm
        uses: azure/setup-helm@v4
        with: { version: "${{ env.HELM_VERSION }}" }
      - name: Helm upgrade
        id: helm
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          aws eks update-kubeconfig --name "${{ matrix.cluster }}" --region "${{ matrix.region }}"
          EXTRA=""
          if [[ "${{ inputs.dry_run }}" == "true" ]]; then EXTRA="--dry-run=server"; fi
          # NOTE: --atomic rolls back on failure; the timeout must exceed the readiness budget (see INC-2291)
          helm upgrade --install kestrel-gateway deploy/charts/gateway \
            --namespace gateway --create-namespace \
            -f deploy/values/${{ env.TARGET_ENV }}.yaml -f deploy/values/${{ matrix.region }}.yaml \
            --set image.tag=${{ needs.build.outputs.image_tag }} \
            --set canary.enabled=${{ matrix.canary }},canary.weight=${{ matrix.weight }} \
            --atomic --timeout 10m $EXTRA
          echo "revision=$(helm history kestrel-gateway -n gateway -o json | jq -r '.[-1].revision')" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - name: Wait for rollout
        run: kubectl -n gateway rollout status deploy/kestrel-gateway --timeout=600s && kubectl -n gateway get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/name=kestrel-gateway -o wide

  canary-analysis:
    needs: deploy
    if: ${{ needs.deploy.result == 'success' && contains(fromJSON('["prod"]'), env.TARGET_ENV) }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
    steps:
      - name: Query error budget burn
        id: burn
        run: |
          q='sum(rate(router_http_requests_total{status=~"5..",env="prod"}[5m])) / sum(rate(router_http_requests_total{env="prod"}[5m]))'
          ratio=$(curl -sG "${PROM_URL}/api/v1/query" --data-urlencode "query=${q}" -H "Authorization: Bearer ${PROM_TOKEN}" | jq -r '.data.result[0].value[1] // "0"')
          echo "ratio=${ratio}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          python3 -c "import sys; sys.exit(0 if float('${ratio}') < 0.002 else 1)"
        env:
          PROM_URL: https://prometheus.ops.kestrel.dev
          PROM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.PROM_READ_TOKEN }}

  notify:
    needs: [deploy, canary-analysis]
    if: "!cancelled() && (needs.deploy.result == 'failure' || needs.canary-analysis.result == 'failure')"
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: slackapi/slack-github-action@v1.26.0
        with:
          channel-id: 'C04PLATFORMSRE'
          payload: '{"text":":rotating_light: Deploy of ${{ github.sha }} to ${{ env.TARGET_ENV }} failed","blocks":[{"type":"section","text":{"type":"mrkdwn","text":"*Run:* <${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}|#${{ github.run_number }}>"}}]}'
        env:
          SLACK_BOT_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SLACK_BOT_TOKEN }}

    scaleTargetRef: {apiVersion: apps/v1, kind: Deployment, name: kestrel-gateway}
    minReplicas: 12
    maxReplicas: 60
    metrics:
        - type: Resource
          resource:
              name: cpu
              target: {type: Utilization, averageUtilization: 55}
        - type: Pods
          pods:
              metric:
                  name: router_http_requests_in_flight
              target:
                  type: AverageValue
                  averageValue: "120"
    behavior:
        scaleUp:
            stabilizationWindowSeconds: 0
            policies:
            - {type: Percent, value: 100, periodSeconds: 30}
            - {type: Pods,value: 8,periodSeconds: 30}
        scaleDown:
            stabilizationWindowSeconds: 600   # flapped during INC-2291, keep this high
            policies: [{type: Percent, value: 10, periodSeconds: 60}]
---

annotations:
    deployment.kubernetes.io/revision: "41"
    reloader.stakater.com/auto: "true"
spec:
  replicas: 12
  revisionHistoryLimit: 5
  strategy:

- name: TRITON_MODEL_VERSION_POLICY
          value: '{"latest": {"num_versions": 2}}'
      resources:
        limits: {cpu: "4", memory: 16Gi, nvidia.com/gpu: "1"}
        requests:
          cpu: "2"
          memory: 12Gi
---

openapi: 3.0.3
info:
  title: Kestrel Control Plane API
  version: "2.4.0"
  # fmt: markdown
  description: |
    Internal API used by `kestrelctl`, the admin UI, and a growing number of scripts nobody admits to owning.
    It manages **feature flags**, **model deployments** and **regional failover**.

    ## Auth
    Every endpoint needs a bearer token from the internal IdP, *except* `/healthz`.
    Tokens are scoped:
    * `flags:read` / `flags:write`
    * `models:deploy` -- only granted to the ML-infra on-call
    rotation
    * `regions:failover` (break glass, audited, pages the IC)

    ## Rate limits
    100 req/s per token, burst 200. Over the limit you get a `429` with a `Retry-After` header; please actually honor it, the gateway team is watching.
  contact: {name: Platform SRE, url: "https://handbook.kestrel.internal/oncall/", email: platform-sre@kestrel.dev}
servers:
- url: https://control.{region}.kestrel.dev/v2
  description: Production (per region)
  variables:
    region:
      enum: [ us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-2 ]
      default: us-east-1
- url: http://localhost:8070/v2
  description: local (docker compose)
security:
  - bearerAuth: []
tags:
  - {name: flags, description: Feature flag definitions and rollouts}
  - {name: models,  description: "Model registry + serving deployments"}
  - name: regions
    description: Regional health and failover. Every call here is audited, and any state change pages the on-call engineer for the affected region.
paths:
  /flags:
    get:
      tags: [flags]
      summary: List flags
      operationId: listFlags
      parameters:
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/Cursor'
        - $ref: "#/components/parameters/Limit"
        - name: state
          in: query
          schema: {type: string, enum: [ENABLED, DISABLED, ARCHIVED]}
        - name: q
          in: query
          description: Substring match on key or description (case-insensitive). Supports a `prefix:` qualifier, e.g. `prefix:gateway.` to list every gateway flag.
          schema:
            type: string
            maxLength: 128
      responses:
        '200':
          description: A page of flags
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                properties:
                  items:
                    type: array
                    items: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Flag'}
                  next_cursor: {type: string, nullable: true}
        "401": {$ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized"}
    post:
      tags: [flags]
      summary: Create a flag
      operationId: createFlag
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/FlagCreate'}
            example: {"key": "gateway.query-planner-v2", "description": "New query planner",
                      "kind": "boolean", "variants": {"on": true, "off": false}, "default_variant": "off"}
      responses:
        201:
          description: Created
          headers:
            Location:
              schema: {type: string, format: uri}
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Flag'
        409:
          description: Flag key already exists
  /flags/{flagKey}/rollout:
    parameters:
      - $ref: '#/components/parameters/FlagKey'
    put:
      tags: [ flags ]
      summary: Change rollout percentage
      description: Sets the absolute percentage of traffic that gets the `on` variant.
        Changes are applied to the canary region first and propagate to the
        remaining regions only after the canary has been healthy for `bake_minutes`.
      operationId: setFlagRollout
      requestBody:
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: '#/components/schemas/RolloutChange'
            examples:
              ramp:
                summary: ramp to 25% in all regions
                value:
                  percentage: 25
                  regions: []
                  bake_minutes: 15
              rollback:
                summary: "Emergency rollback"
                value: {percentage: 0, regions: [eu-west-1], bake_minutes: 0, reason: "INC-2291: elevated 5xx"}
      responses:
        '202':
          description: Accepted; poll the returned operation.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: '#/components/schemas/Operation' }
        '422': {description: Validation error, content: {application/problem+json: {schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Problem'}}}}
  /models/{modelName}/deployments:
    post:
      tags: [models]
      summary: Deploy a model version
      operationId: deployModel
      parameters:
      - name: modelName
        in: path
        required: true
        schema:
          type: string
          pattern: "^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{2,40}$"
      requestBody:
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [version, strategy]
              properties:
                version:
                  type: string
                  pattern: "^v\\d+(\\.\\d+){0,2}(-rc\\.\\d+)?$"
                  example: v7.2.0-rc.1
                strategy:
                  type: string
                  enum: [canary, blue_green, shadow]
                  default: canary
                canary:
                  type: object
                  properties:
                    traffic_percent:
                      type: integer
                      minimum: 0
                      maximum: 100
                      description: Percentage of traffic (0-100) routed to the new version
                        before automatic promotion. Ignored when strategy is blue_green.
                    promote_after: {type: string, format: duration, example: "PT30M"}
                    guardrails:
                      type: array
                      items:
                        type: object
                        properties:
                          metric: {type: string, enum: [p99_latency_ms, error_rate, gpu_util, "ndcg@10"]}
                          op: {type: string, enum: ['<', '<=', '>', '>=']}
                          threshold: {type: number}
      responses:
        '202':
          description: Deployment started
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Operation'}
components:
  securitySchemes:
    bearerAuth: {type: http, scheme: bearer, bearerFormat: JWT}
    oauth:
      type: oauth2
      flows:
        clientCredentials:
          tokenUrl: https://idp.kestrel.internal/oauth2/token
          scopes:
            flags:read: Read flags
            flags:write: Create/modify flags
            models:deploy: Deploy model versions
            regions:failover: "Break-glass: fail a region over"
  parameters:
    FlagKey:
      name: flagKey
      in: path
      required: true
      schema: {type: string, pattern: '^[a-z0-9]+(\.[a-z0-9-]+)+$'}
      example: gateway.apq-enforce
    Cursor: {name: cursor, in: query, schema: {type: string}}
    Limit:
      name: limit
      in: query
      schema: {type: integer, minimum: 1, maximum: 500, default: 50}
  responses:
    Unauthorized:
      description: Missing or invalid token

          description: Substring match on key or description (case-insensitive). Supports a `prefix:` qualifier, e.g. `prefix:gateway.` to list every gateway flag.
          schema:
            type: string
            maxLength: 128
      responses:
        '200':
          description: A page of flags
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                properties:
                  items:
                    type: array
                    items: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Flag'}
                  next_cursor: {type: string, nullable: true}
        "401": {description: Missing or invalid token}
    post:
      tags: [flags]
      summary: Create a flag
      operationId: createFlag
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/FlagCreate'}
            example: {"key": "gateway.query-planner-v2", "description": "New query planner",
                      "kind": "boolean", "variants": {"on": true, "off": false}, "default_variant": "off"}
      responses:
        201:
          description: Created
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Flag'
        409:
          description: Flag key already exists
  /flags/{flagKey}/rollout:
    parameters:
      - $ref: '#/components/parameters/FlagKey'
    put:
      tags: [ flags ]
      summary: Change rollout percentage
      description: Sets the absolute percentage of traffic that gets the `on` variant.
        Changes are applied to the canary region first and propagate to the
        remaining regions only after the canary has been healthy for `bake_minutes`.
      operationId: setFlagRollout
      requestBody:
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: '#/components/schemas/RolloutChange'
            examples:
              ramp:
                summary: ramp to 25% in all regions
                value:
                  percentage: 25
                  regions: []
                  bake_minutes: 15
              rollback:
                summary: "Emergency rollback"
                value: {percentage: 0, regions: [eu-west-1], bake_minutes: 0, reason: "INC-2291: elevated 5xx"}
      responses:
        '202':
          description: Accepted; poll the returned operation.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: '#/components/schemas/Operation' }
        '422': {description: Validation error, content: {application/problem+json: {schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Problem'}}}}
  /models/{modelName}/deployments:
    post:
      tags: [models]
      summary: Deploy a model version
      operationId: deployModel
      parameters:
      - name: modelName
        in: path
        required: true
        schema:
          type: string
          pattern: "^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{2,40}$"
      requestBody:
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [version, strategy]
              properties:
                version:
                  type: string
                  pattern: "^v\\d+(\\.\\d+){0,2}(-rc\\.\\d+)?$"
                  example: v7.2.0-rc.1
                strategy:
                  type: string
                  enum: [canary, blue_green, shadow]
                  default: canary
                canary:
                  type: object
                  properties:
                    traffic_percent:
                      type: integer
                      minimum: 0
                      maximum: 100
                      description: Percentage of traffic (0-100) routed to the new version
                        before automatic promotion. Ignored when strategy is blue_green.
                    promote_after: {type: string, format: duration, example: "PT30M"}
                    guardrails:
                      type: array
                      items:
                        type: object
                        properties:
                          metric: {type: string, enum: [p99_latency_ms, error_rate, gpu_util, "ndcg@10"]}
                          op: {type: string, enum: ['<', '<=', '>', '>=']}
                          threshold: {type: number}
      responses:
        '202': {description: Deployment started, content: {application/json: {schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Operation'}}}}
components:
  securitySchemes:
    bearerAuth: {type: http, scheme: bearer, bearerFormat: JWT}
    oauth:
      type: oauth2
      flows:
        clientCredentials:
          tokenUrl: https://idp.kestrel.internal/oauth2/token
          scopes:
            flags:read: Read flags
            flags:write: Create/modify flags
            models:deploy: Deploy model versions
            regions:failover: "Break-glass: fail a region over"
  parameters:
    FlagKey:
      name: flagKey
      in: path
      required: true
      schema: {type: string, pattern: '^[a-z0-9]+(\.[a-z0-9-]+)+$'}
      example: gateway.apq-enforce
    Cursor: {name: cursor, in: query, schema: {type: string}}
    Limit: {name: limit, in: query, schema: {type: integer, minimum: 1, maximum: 500, default: 50}}
  schemas:
    Flag:
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/FlagCreate'
        - type: object
          required: [state, created_at]
          properties:
            state: {type: string, enum: [ ENABLED, DISABLED, ARCHIVED ]}
            created_at: {type: string, format: date-time, example: "2024-10-21T09:14:00Z"}
            rollout:
              type: object
              properties:
                percentage: {type: number, minimum: 0, maximum: 100, example: 12.5}
                by_region:
                  type: object
                  additionalProperties: {type: number}
                  example: {us-east-1: 25, eu-west-1: 0, ap-southeast-2: 25}
    FlagCreate:
      type: object
      required: [key, kind, variants, default_variant]
      properties:
        key: {type: string, example: gateway.query-planner-v2}
        description: {type: string, maxLength: 500}
        kind: {type: string, enum: [boolean, string, number, json]}
        variants:
          type: object
          additionalProperties: true
          example: {"on": true, "off": false}
        default_variant: {type: string, example: "off"}
        targeting:
          type: object
          nullable: true
          description: JsonLogic rule evaluated by flagd. Must be valid JsonLogic -- the admin API runs it against a sample context before saving and rejects rules that throw.
    RolloutChange:
      type: object
      required: [percentage]
      properties:
        percentage: {type: number, minimum: 0, maximum: 100}
        regions: {type: array, items: {type: string, enum: [us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-2]}, description: "Empty = all regions"}
        bake_minutes: {type: integer, default: 15}
        reason: {type: string}
    Operation:
      type: object
      properties: {id: {type: string, format: uuid}, status: {type: string, enum: [pending, running, succeeded, failed, rolled_back]}}
    Problem: {type: object, properties: {type: {type: string, format: uri, default: "about:blank"}, title: {type: string}, status: {type: integer, example: 422}}}

kestrel/platform

Platform monorepo for Kestrel: infrastructure-as-code for all three regions, the GraphQL gateway (Apollo Router plus our Rust plugins), the feature flag service (flagd, plus a sync job from the old LaunchDarkly export that we keep promising to delete), and the model-serving stack (Triton on KServe). If you are here because something is on fire, skip straight to [Runbooks](#runbooks) :fire: and page `#platform-sre`. Everything else: read on. ## Contents * [Quickstart](#quickstart) * [Repository layout](#repository-layout) * [Running the *gateway* locally](#running-the-gateway-locally-with-make-dev) + [Feature flags](#feature-flags) * [Runbooks](#runbooks) ## Quickstart You need Docker (or OrbStack), `kubectl` >= 1.29, `helm` 3.15+ and AWS SSO access to the `kestrel-dev` account. On macOS: ```console $ brew bundle --file=Brewfile $ make bootstrap ==> checking docker........ ok ==> checking aws sso....... ok (expires in 7h59m) ==> pulling images (this takes a while the first time) $ make dev [+] Running 7/7 ✔ Container kestrel-dev-postgres-1 Healthy ✔ Container kestrel-gateway Started ``` ```bash title="scripts/dev-env.sh" linenums="1" export AWS_PROFILE=kestrel-dev export KESTREL_REGION="${KESTREL_REGION:-us-east-1}" aws sso login --profile "$AWS_PROFILE" || { echo "sso login failed" >&2; exit 1; } ``` > **Heads up:** `make bootstrap` rewrites the `kestrel-*` contexts in your kubeconfig. Back it up first if you have hand-edited contexts: > ```sh > cp ~/.kube/config ~/.kube/config.bak.$(date +%s) > ``` > Restore it with `mv` if anything looks off. ## Repository layout | Path | What | Owner | |---|---|---| | `deploy/charts/` | Helm charts (gateway, flagd, model-sync) | platform-sre | | `deploy/k8s/` | Raw manifests that haven't been chart-ified yet :grimacing: | platform-sre | | `services/gateway/`| Router config + Rust plugins (auth, cost limits, persisted queries) | [gateway team](https://github.com/orgs/kestrel/teams/gateway) | `services/flags-sync/` | LaunchDarkly → flagd sync job (deprecated, see [ADR-014](docs/adr/014-flagd.md)) | platform-sre | `ml/serving/` | KServe `InferenceService` specs + Triton `config.pbtxt` files | ml-infra | | `tools/rollout/` |`rollout.py`, the CLI for progressive flag rollouts| platform-sre | Region | Role | Cluster | Notes --- | :---: | --- | --- us-east-1 | primary + canary | `prod-use1-blue` | gets every gateway and flag change first eu-west-1 | primary (EU data) | `prod-euw1-blue` | see the [INC-2291 post-mortem]( "Gateway brownout, Oct 2024") ap-southeast-2 | secondary | `prod-apse2-a` | no GPU nodes yet; inference falls back to us-east-1 (~180ms extra) ## Running the *gateway* locally with `make dev` The gateway reads `services/gateway/router.yaml` plus a composed supergraph. When you change a subgraph schema you have to recompose before restarting, otherwise the router happily keeps serving the old schema and you will lose an afternoon like I did. ```yaml # services/gateway/router.local.yaml -- overrides for laptops supergraph: listen: 127.0.0.1:4000 introspection: True headers: all: request: - propagate: {matching: "^x-kestrel-.*"} include_subgraph_errors: { all: true } ``` Restart with Ctrl+C and `make dev` again; hot reload only watches `router.yaml`, not the supergraph. ## Feature flags Flags live in `flags/flags.yaml` and are served by [flagd] in every region. The workflow: 1. Edit `flags/flags.yaml` (or use `tools/rollout/rollout.py`) - flag keys are `.` in kebab-case - every flag needs an `owner` and an `expires` date, CI fails otherwise 2. Open a PR. The `flags-lint` job evaluates the JsonLogic rules against a sample context and posts a diff of the evaluated variants for ~2k synthetic users. 3. After merge flagd picks up the change within ~30s * staging first, then the canary region, then the rest * need it faster? `kubectl -n flags rollout restart deploy/flagd` -- but not during business hours please | Region | Gateway p99 | Flag eval p99 | |----------------|------------:|--------------:| | us-east-1 | 182 ms | 1.9 ms | | eu-west-1 | 240 ms | 2.4 ms | | ap-southeast-2 | 311 ms | 3.1 ms | * numbers from the October load test, pasted into the quarterly deck as-is, please don't reformat ## Runbooks ## - [Gateway: restart / drain](docs/runbooks/gateway/restart.md) - [Gateway: subgraph timeouts]() - [Flags: flagd returns defaults everywhere](docs/runbooks/flags.md#everything-is-default "the scary one") - [GPU nodes stuck `NotReady`](docs/runbooks/gpu-notready.md) The gateway enforces persisted queries in production[^apq] and a per-operation cost limit[^cost]. If you see `PERSISTED_QUERY_NOT_IN_LIST` in staging, that is a client bug, not ours.
Why no service mesh for the gateway? We tried Istio in 2023. Short version: an extra hop, ~4ms of p50, and a sidecar that OOMed under the query-planner warmup. Details in [ADR-009](docs/adr/009-no-mesh-for-gateway.md).
## Roadmap (Q4) - [x] Persisted queries enforced on the public gateway - [x] KServe 0.13 upgrade - [ ] Delete the LaunchDarkly sync job :skull: - [ ] ap-southeast-2 GPU pool - [ ] quota request for `g5` instances - [X] Triton model warmup on scale-up - [ ] Active-active writes for the flags DB (needs an ADR first) Contributing ------------ Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) first. TL;DR: small PRs, a ticket number in the title, and never `kubectl edit` in prod without writing it down in the incident channel. More background reading: the [Apollo Router docs][router], [flagd][], and the [KServe docs][kserve] (we use `RawDeployment` mode, so ignore everything about Knative). [router]: https://www.apollographql.com/docs/router/ "Apollo Router" [flagd]: https://flagd.dev/ [kserve]: 'KServe documentation' [^apq]: Automatic persisted queries are still allowed in staging so that Apollo Studio Explorer keeps working. In prod the router rejects unknown hashes. [^cost]: Cost is estimated from the static query plan, not measured at runtime. See `services/gateway/plugins/cost_limit.rs` if you want to argue about the weights.

title:   "Contributing to kestrel/platform"
description: How we review, test and ship changes to the platform monorepo (infra, the GraphQL gateway, feature flags and model serving). Read this before your first PR, it will save you a round of review.
sidebar_position: 2
tags: [ contributing,process,  on-call ]
owners:
    - "@kestrel/platform-sre"
    - '@kestrel/ml-infra'
last_reviewed: 2024-10-02
draft: False
---

# Contributing

Thanks for helping keep the platform upright! :wave: This page covers the boring-but-important parts: how to set up, how we name things, what a reviewable PR looks like and how releases go out. It is opinionated because almost every rule here exists because of a specific incident.

## Ground rules

- **Small PRs.** Under ~400 changed lines unless it is generated code. Big refactors get split or get an ADR
first.
- Every PR title starts with a ticket: `PLAT-1234: ...`. Hotfixes during an incident can use the incident id instead (`INC-2291: ...`).
- Don't `kubectl apply` or `kubectl edit` against prod from your laptop. If you absolutely have to (you are the IC, the pipeline is down, etc.) write down every command in the incident channel *as you run it*.
-   Feature flags are not a substitute for a rollback plan.

## Local setup

1. Install the toolchain:
   ```console
   $ brew bundle --file=Brewfile
   $ uv tool install pre-commit && pre-commit install --install-hooks
   ```
2. Log in to AWS SSO (`aws sso login --profile kestrel-dev`) and run `make bootstrap`.
3) Run `make dev` and check that <http://localhost:4000> serves the sandbox.

Pre-commit runs `ruff`, `yamllint`, `helm lint`, `shellcheck` and `yamark format --check`. If a hook rewrites files, just `git add` them and commit again -- that is not a failure.


## Commits and branches

We use [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/) because the changelog generator depends on it.

| Type | When | Shows up in changelog? |
| ---- | ---- | :---: |
| `feat` | new user-visible behaviour (a new flag kind, a new region) | yes |
| `fix` | bug fixes, including config fixes | yes |
| `perf`|latency / cost improvements, with numbers in the PR description | yes |
| `chore` | deps, CI, tooling | no |
| `revert` | reverting a previous commit (use `git revert`, keep the generated message) | yes |

```text title="example commit message"
fix(gateway): lower subgraph timeout to 2.5s

The 10s default let a single slow subgraph pin every router worker during
INC-2291. 2.5s is above the p99.9 of every subgraph over the last 30 days.

Refs: INC-2291, PLAT-1877
```

## Pull request checklist

Copy this into the PR description if the template didn't load:

- [ ] Ticket id in the title
- [ ] `make test` passes locally
- [ ] Dashboards / alerts updated if you renamed a metric
- [ ] New flags have an `owner` and an `expires` date
- [x] I read this document :)

## Feature flags

> Flags are config, not code. Treat a flag flip like a deploy.
>
> ```yaml
> gateway.query-planner-v2:
>     state: ENABLED
>     owner: gateway-team
>     expires: 2025-01-31
>     variants: {on: true,off: false}
>     defaultVariant: off
> ```

Some rules that came out of the last two quarters of incidents:

* Name flags `<service>.<feature>`, lowercase, kebab-case after the dot.
* Default to `off`. A flag that defaults to `on` is a deploy in disguise
  and has to go through the normal release review.
* Remove flags within two sprints of reaching 100%. The `flags-janitor` bot opens a PR for every flag past its `expires` date; please don't just bump the date.

## Tests

```console
$ make test                       # unit tests, ~2 min
$ pytest tools/rollout -k "ramp and not slow" -q
$ k6 run load/gateway-smoke.js --vus 20 --duration 60s
```

Schema changes need a contract test. The GraphQL type for flags currently looks like this:

```graphql
type Flag { key: ID!  state: FlagState!
    variants: JSON  rollout:Rollout }
```

<!-- fmt: skip -->
| Check          | Where                | Blocking? |
|----------------|----------------------|-----------|
| unit           | GitHub Actions       | yes       |
| schema diff    | `graphql-inspector`  | yes       |
| load smoke     | nightly, staging     | no        |

## Releasing

The gateway chart and `rollout.py` are versioned with SemVer; everything else ships continuously.

1. Merge to `main`. The `build-and-deploy` workflow deploys to staging automatically
2. Cut a release:
    1. `make release VERSION=2.15.0` bumps `Chart.yaml` and moves the changelog entries
    2. push the tag: `git push origin v2.15.0`
3. Approve the prod deployment in the GitHub environment. The canary region goes first; if the error-budget check fails, the workflow rolls back by itself and pings `#platform-sre`.

## Code review expectations

Reviewers try to respond within one business day[^sla]. If your PR blocks an incident follow-up, say so in the title and ping the on-call reviewer directly instead of the whole channel. See the [review guide](<docs/process/code review.md> "How we review") for what we look at.



[^sla]: "Business day" in the reviewer's time zone. We have people in three of them, so a PR opened on Friday afternoon in Sydney may sit until Monday in Dublin.

# Changelog
All notable changes to `kestrel/platform` are documented in this file. The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and the gateway chart plus `rollout.py` adhere to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html); infra-only changes are listed under whichever release they shipped with.



## [Unreleased]
### Added
- `rollout.py ramp --schedule` to ramp a flag on a cron-like schedule instead of babysitting it ([#1501](https://github.com/kestrel/platform/pull/1501))
- ap-southeast-2: GPU node pool behind the `infra.gpu-apse2` flag, scaled to zero until the quota request
lands
### Changed
* Gateway subgraph timeout lowered from 10s to 2.5s (INC-2291 action item 3). If you own a subgraph that legitimately needs longer, talk to us before adding a per-subgraph override.

## [2.14.0] - 2024-11-08
### :boom: Breaking
- The gateway chart no longer creates the `apollo-studio` secret. Create it yourself (or via external-secrets) **before** upgrading:
  ```diff
  - router:
  -   studio:
  -     createSecret: true
  + router:
  +   studio:
  +     existingSecret: apollo-studio
  ```
- `rollout.py` exits with code `3` (was `1`) when a guardrail trips, so CI can tell "rolled back" apart from "crashed".

### Added
- Persisted query enforcement in prod :tada: Unknown operations now get `PERSISTED_QUERY_NOT_IN_LIST` instead of being executed. The safelist is published by the `pq-publish` job on every client release.
- KServe `InferenceService` for `ranker_v7` with canary support, see `ml/serving/ranker-v7.yaml`
- Grafana dashboard *Gateway / Subgraph latency* (uid `gw-subgraph-lat`)
### Fixed
- flagd sidecar no longer crash-loops when the flags ConfigMap is empty during a rolling update (#1466)
- `model-sync` CronJob: `aws s3 sync` used `--delete` against the wrong prefix in ap-southeast-2 and wiped the
  warm cache every 15 minutes. Nobody noticed because there are no GPU nodes there yet. :see_no_evil:
- HPA for the gateway now scales on in-flight requests as well as CPU; CPU alone reacted ~4 min too late during INC-2291[^hpa]

### **Security**
- Bump Apollo Router to `v1.52.0` (upstream advisory: query depth limit bypass via nested fragment spreads)
- Rotate the `PROM_READ_TOKEN` used by the canary analysis job, the old one was printed in a debug log for ~3 days.

## [2.13.2] - 2024-10-24
### Fixed
1. Hotfixes from INC-2291:
    - raise `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` to 45s so in-flight requests drain
    - PDB `minAvailable` 80% (was 50%)
2. Revert "use the new query planner by default" -- it is back behind `gateway.query-planner-v2` at 10%

## [2.13.1] - 2024-10-03
### Changed
- Model sync now uses `--exact-timestamps`. Without it `aws s3 sync` skipped re-uploaded models with the same size, which is exactly what happens when you re-export an ONNX graph with different weights. Lovely.

### Deprecated
The following flags are deprecated and will be removed in **2.16.0**:

| flag | replacement | notes |
|------|-------------|-------|
| `gateway.legacy-auth` | none | removed once mobile 5.x is below 1% of traffic
| `ml.ranker-v6` | `ml.ranker-v7` | |
| `flags.ld-sync-enabled` | – | the LaunchDarkly sync job goes away with it |

## [2.13.0] - 2024-09-19
### Added
+ Multi-region flag evaluation: flagd runs in every region and syncs from the same S3 bucket. Evaluation latency p99 went from 41ms (cross-region call to us-east-1) to under 3ms.
+ Helm values for per-region overrides, e.g.:

  ```yaml
  # deploy/values/eu-west-1.yaml
  router:
      replicas: 8
      env:
        - {name: KESTREL_REGION, value: eu-west-1}
        - {name: DATA_RESIDENCY,   value: "eu"}
  ```

### Changed
- Minimum Kubernetes version is now 1.28.  
- `kestrel-gateway` image is multi-arch (amd64 + arm64); the arm64 nodes in us-east-1 are ~22% cheaper
  for the same throughput, so new node pools default to Graviton.
- Renamed metric `gateway_requests_total` → `router_http_requests_total` to match upstream. Dashboards were updated, your ad-hoc queries were not.


## [2.12.0] - 2024-08-30
_First release tracked in this file._ Earlier history lives in the wiki: <https://wiki.kestrel.internal/platform/history>.

# Changelog
All notable changes to `kestrel/platform` are documented in this file. The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and the gateway chart plus `rollout.py` adhere to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html); infra-only changes are listed under whichever release they shipped with.



## [Unreleased]
### Added
- `rollout.py ramp --schedule` to ramp a flag on a cron-like schedule instead of babysitting it ([#1501](https://github.com/kestrel/platform/pull/1501))
- ap-southeast-2: GPU node pool behind the `infra.gpu-apse2` flag, scaled to zero until the quota request
lands
### Changed
* Gateway subgraph timeout lowered from 10s to 2.5s (INC-2291 action item 3). If you own a subgraph that legitimately needs longer, talk to us before adding a per-subgraph override.

## [2.14.0] - 2024-11-08
### :boom: Breaking
- The gateway chart no longer creates the `apollo-studio` secret. Create it yourself (or via external-secrets) **before** upgrading:
  ```diff
  - router:
  -   studio:
  -     createSecret: true
  + router:
  +   studio:
  +     existingSecret: apollo-studio
  ```
- `rollout.py` exits with code `3` (was `1`) when a guardrail trips, so CI can tell "rolled back" apart from "crashed".

### Added
- Persisted query enforcement in prod :tada: Unknown operations now get `PERSISTED_QUERY_NOT_IN_LIST` instead of being executed. The safelist is published by the `pq-publish` job on every client release.
- KServe `InferenceService` for `ranker_v7` with canary support, see `ml/serving/ranker-v7.yaml`
- Grafana dashboard *Gateway / Subgraph latency* (uid `gw-subgraph-lat`)
### Fixed
- flagd sidecar no longer crash-loops when the flags ConfigMap is empty during a rolling update (#1466)
- `model-sync` CronJob: `aws s3 sync` used `--delete` against the wrong prefix in ap-southeast-2 and wiped the
  warm cache every 15 minutes. Nobody noticed because there are no GPU nodes there yet. :see_no_evil:
- HPA for the gateway now scales on in-flight requests as well as CPU; CPU alone reacted ~4 min too late during INC-2291[^hpa]

### **Security**
- Bump Apollo Router to `v1.52.0` (upstream advisory: query depth limit bypass via nested fragment spreads)
- Rotate the `PROM_READ_TOKEN` used by the canary analysis job, the old one was printed in a debug log for ~3 days.

## [2.13.2] - 2024-10-24
### Fixed
1. Hotfixes from INC-2291:
    - raise `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` to 45s so in-flight requests drain
    - PDB `minAvailable` 80% (was 50%)
2. Revert "use the new query planner by default" -- it is back behind `gateway.query-planner-v2` at 10%

## [2.13.1] - 2024-10-03
### Changed
- Model sync now uses `--exact-timestamps`. Without it `aws s3 sync` skipped re-uploaded models with the same size, which is exactly what happens when you re-export an ONNX graph with different weights. Lovely.

### Deprecated
The following flags are deprecated and will be removed in **2.16.0**:

| flag | replacement | notes |
|------|-------------|-------|
| `gateway.legacy-auth` | none | removed once mobile 5.x is below 1% of traffic
| `ml.ranker-v6` | `ml.ranker-v7` | |
| `flags.ld-sync-enabled` | – | the LaunchDarkly sync job goes away with it |

## [2.13.0] - 2024-09-19
### Added
+ Multi-region flag evaluation: flagd runs in every region and syncs from the same S3 bucket. Evaluation latency p99 went from 41ms (cross-region call to us-east-1) to under 3ms.
+ Helm values for per-region overrides, e.g.:

  ```yaml
  # deploy/values/eu-west-1.yaml
  router:
      replicas: 8
      env:
        - {name: KESTREL_REGION, value: eu-west-1}
        - {name: DATA_RESIDENCY,   value: "eu"}
  ```

### Changed
- Minimum Kubernetes version is now 1.28.  
- `kestrel-gateway` image is multi-arch (amd64 + arm64); the arm64 nodes in us-east-1 are ~22% cheaper
  for the same throughput, so new node pools default to Graviton.
- Renamed metric `gateway_requests_total` → `router_http_requests_total` to match upstream. Dashboards were updated, your ad-hoc queries were not.


## [2.12.0] - 2024-08-30
_First release tracked in this file._ Earlier history lives in the wiki: <https://wiki.kestrel.internal/platform/history>.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""rollout.py - progressive feature-flag rollouts for the Kestrel platform.

Talks to the flagd management API in each region and ramps a flag through a
list of percentages, checking the gateway 5xx ratio between steps.
Written mostly during the INC-2291 week, so the tests (tools/rollout/tests) are thin.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import logging
import os
import random
import sys
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request
from typing import Sequence

log = logging.getLogger("rollout")

# fmt: markdown
# ## How a ramp works
# Each step sets the *absolute* percentage of the `on` variant (not a delta), waits `--bake` minutes,
# then asks Prometheus for the gateway 5xx ratio in that region. If the
# ratio is above `--max-error-ratio` we put the flag back to the previous step and exit with code 3.
#
# Regions are always processed in this order:
# 1. the canary region (`us-east-1`)
# 2. everything else, one region at a time
#    - unless `--parallel` is passed, which you should only ever do in staging
#
# Retry/backoff is lifted from a Stack Overflow answer (full jitter, capped at 30s); see `_request`.

DEFAULT_REGIONS = ("us-east-1", "eu-west-1", "ap-southeast-2")
CANARY_REGION = "us-east-1"
FLAGD_URL_TMPL = os.environ.get("FLAGD_URL_TMPL", "https://flags.{region}.kestrel.internal")
PROM_URL = os.environ.get("PROM_URL", "https://prometheus.ops.kestrel.dev")
EXIT_OK, EXIT_USAGE, EXIT_ROLLED_BACK, EXIT_UNREACHABLE = 0, 2, 3, 4

# %% [markdown]
# Step tables. Hand-aligned on purpose: ruff and yamark must leave this cell alone.

# fmt: off
# %%
#| label: step-tables
#| tags:   [config,   do-not-format]
DEFAULT_STEPS = [1,   5,  10,  25,  50, 100]
BAKE_MINUTES  = {"staging": 2,     "prod": 15}
ERROR_RATIO   = {"staging": 0.02,  "prod": 0.002}
# fmt: on

# fmt: markdown
EPILOG = """
Examples
========

Ramp the new query planner in staging with five minutes between steps:

```console
$ rollout.py --env staging ramp gateway.query-planner-v2 --steps 5,25,100 --bake 5
```

Roll a flag back to 0% everywhere (you will be asked to type the flag key to confirm):

```console
$ rollout.py --env prod rollback gateway.apq-enforce --reason "INC-2291"
```

Notes
-----
* Percentages are absolute: `--steps 5,25,100` means 5%, then 25%, then 100% -- not +5/+25.
* `--dry-run` is **on by default** for `--env prod`. Pass `--no-dry-run` once you have an incident commander or an approved change ticket.
* Exit codes:
    0 = done, 2 = bad arguments, 3 = guardrail tripped and the flag was rolled back,
4 = flagd unreachable
"""


def _parse_steps(raw: str) -> list[float]:
    try:
        steps = [float(s) for s in raw.split(",") if s.strip()]
    except ValueError:
        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(f"bad --steps value: {raw!r}")
    if not steps or any(s < 0 or s > 100 for s in steps) or steps != sorted(steps):
        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError("--steps must be increasing percentages between 0 and 100")
    return steps


def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="rollout.py",
        description="Progressive feature-flag rollouts (flagd) with error-budget guardrails.",
        epilog=EPILOG,
        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter,
    )
    p.add_argument("-v", "--verbose", action="count", default=0)
    p.add_argument("--env", choices=["staging", "prod"], default=os.environ.get("KESTREL_ENV", "staging"))
    p.add_argument("--regions", type=lambda s: [r.strip() for r in s.split(",") if r.strip()],
                   default=list(DEFAULT_REGIONS), help="comma separated; the canary region always goes first")
    sub = p.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)

    ramp_p = sub.add_parser("ramp", help="ramp a flag through a list of percentages")
    ramp_p.add_argument("flag")
    ramp_p.add_argument("--steps", type=_parse_steps, default=None, help="e.g. 1,5,25,100")
    ramp_p.add_argument("--bake", type=int, default=None, metavar="MINUTES")
    ramp_p.add_argument("--max-error-ratio", type=float, default=None)
    ramp_p.add_argument("--dry-run", action=argparse.BooleanOptionalAction, default=None)
    ramp_p.add_argument("--parallel", action="store_true", help=argparse.SUPPRESS)

    rb = sub.add_parser("rollback", help="set a flag to 0%% in the given regions")
    rb.add_argument("flag")
    rb.add_argument("--reason", required=True)
    rb.add_argument("--yes", action="store_true", help="skip the confirmation prompt")

    st = sub.add_parser("status", help="print the current rollout per region as JSON")
    st.add_argument("flag", nargs="?")
    return p


def _request(method: str, url: str, body: dict | None = None, *, attempts: int = 5) -> dict:
    data = json.dumps(body).encode() if body is not None else None
    headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json", "Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ.get('FLAGD_ADMIN_TOKEN', '')}"}
    for attempt in range(1, attempts + 1):
        req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=data, method=method, headers=headers)
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=10) as resp:
                return json.loads(resp.read() or b"{}")
        except (urllib.error.URLError, TimeoutError) as exc:
            if attempt == attempts:
                raise
            # full jitter: sleep somewhere in [0, min(cap, base * 2**attempt))
            delay = random.uniform(0, min(30.0, 0.5 * 2 ** attempt))
            log.warning("%s %s failed (%s), retry %d/%d in %.1fs", method, url, exc, attempt, attempts, delay)
            time.sleep(delay)
    raise RuntimeError("unreachable")


def get_rollout(region: str, flag: str) -> float:
    doc = _request("GET", f"{FLAGD_URL_TMPL.format(region=region)}/admin/v1/flags/{flag}")
    return float(doc.get("rollout", {}).get("percentage", 0.0))


def set_rollout(region: str, flag: str, pct: float, *, dry_run: bool, reason: str = "") -> None:
    if dry_run:
        log.info("[dry-run] %s: %s -> %.1f%%", region, flag, pct)
        return
    _request("PUT", f"{FLAGD_URL_TMPL.format(region=region)}/admin/v1/flags/{flag}/rollout",
             {"percentage": pct, "reason": reason or "rollout.py"})


def error_ratio(region: str, window: str = "5m") -> float:
    q = (f'sum(rate(router_http_requests_total{{status=~"5..",region="{region}"}}[{window}]))'
         f' / sum(rate(router_http_requests_total{{region="{region}"}}[{window}]))')
    with urllib.request.urlopen(f"{PROM_URL}/api/v1/query?" + urllib.parse.urlencode({"query": q}), timeout=10) as resp:
        result = json.load(resp)["data"]["result"]
    return float(result[0]["value"][1]) if result else 0.0


def ramp(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    steps = args.steps or DEFAULT_STEPS
    bake = args.bake if args.bake is not None else BAKE_MINUTES[args.env]
    max_err = args.max_error_ratio if args.max_error_ratio is not None else ERROR_RATIO[args.env]
    dry_run = args.dry_run if args.dry_run is not None else args.env == "prod"
    for region in [CANARY_REGION] + [r for r in args.regions if r != CANARY_REGION]:
        current = get_rollout(region, args.flag)
        for pct in (s for s in steps if s > current):
            set_rollout(region, args.flag, pct, dry_run=dry_run)
            if dry_run:
                continue
            time.sleep(bake * 60)
            ratio = error_ratio(region)
            if ratio > max_err:
                log.error("%s: 5xx ratio %.4f > %.4f at %.1f%%, rolling back to %.1f%%", region, ratio, max_err, pct, current)
                set_rollout(region, args.flag, current, dry_run=False, reason=f"guardrail: ratio={ratio:.4f}")
                return EXIT_ROLLED_BACK
            current = pct
    return EXIT_OK


def rollback(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    if not args.yes and input(f"type the flag key to roll back {args.flag!r} everywhere: ").strip() != args.flag:
        print("aborted", file=sys.stderr)
        return EXIT_USAGE
    for region in args.regions:
        set_rollout(region, args.flag, 0.0, dry_run=False, reason=args.reason)
    return EXIT_OK


def status(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    json.dump({r: get_rollout(r, args.flag) for r in args.regions} if args.flag else {}, sys.stdout, indent=2)
    print()
    return EXIT_OK


def main(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> int:
    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG if args.verbose > 1 else logging.INFO if args.verbose else logging.WARNING,
                        format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(message)s")
    try:
        return {"ramp": ramp, "rollback": rollback, "status": status}[args.cmd](args)
    except urllib.error.URLError as exc:
        log.error("flagd unreachable: %s", exc)
        return EXIT_UNREACHABLE


# %% [markdown]
# ## Scratch
# Run these in the VS Code interactive window, or `quarto render tools/rollout/rollout.py`,
# to eyeball the step tables before touching prod. Guarded so the CLI never runs them.

# %%
#| label: preview-steps
#| echo:   false
#| output:  asis
#| tags: [ "scratch",preview ]
if os.environ.get("ROLLOUT_SCRATCH"):
    for env in ("staging", "prod"):
        print(f"| {env} | {DEFAULT_STEPS} | {BAKE_MINUTES[env]} min | {ERROR_RATIO[env]} |")

# %%
#| label: fig-burn
#| fig-cap:    "5xx ratio per region during the last ramp"
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height:    3.5
#| warning: False
#| params:
#|     window: 6h
#|     regions: [us-east-1,eu-west-1 , ap-southeast-2]
if os.environ.get("ROLLOUT_SCRATCH"):
    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt  # scratch only

    ratios = {r: error_ratio(r, "6h") for r in DEFAULT_REGIONS}
    plt.bar(list(ratios), list(ratios.values()))
    plt.axhline(ERROR_RATIO["prod"], linestyle="--")
    plt.show()

# %%
if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

         f' / sum(rate(router_http_requests_total{{region="{region}"}}[{window}]))')
    with urllib.request.urlopen(f"{PROM_URL}/api/v1/query?" + urllib.parse.urlencode({"query": q}), timeout=10) as resp:
        result = json.load(resp)["data"]["result"]
    return float(result[0]["value"][1]) if result else 0.0


def ramp(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    steps = args.steps or DEFAULT_STEPS
    bake = args.bake if args.bake is not None else BAKE_MINUTES[args.env]
    max_err = args.max_error_ratio if args.max_error_ratio is not None else ERROR_RATIO[args.env]
    dry_run = args.dry_run if args.dry_run is not None else args.env == "prod"
    for region in [CANARY_REGION] + [r for r in args.regions if r != CANARY_REGION]:
        current = get_rollout(region, args.flag)
        for pct in (s for s in steps if s > current):
            set_rollout(region, args.flag, pct, dry_run=dry_run)
            if dry_run:
                continue
            time.sleep(bake * 60)
            ratio = error_ratio(region)
            if ratio > max_err:
                log.error("%s: 5xx ratio %.4f > %.4f at %.1f%%, rolling back to %.1f%%", region, ratio, max_err, pct, current)
                set_rollout(region, args.flag, current, dry_run=False, reason=f"guardrail: ratio={ratio:.4f}")
                return EXIT_ROLLED_BACK
            current = pct
    return EXIT_OK


def rollback(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    if not args.yes and input(f"type the flag key to roll back {args.flag!r} everywhere: ").strip() != args.flag:
        print("aborted", file=sys.stderr)
        return EXIT_USAGE
    for region in args.regions:
        set_rollout(region, args.flag, 0.0, dry_run=False, reason=args.reason)
    return EXIT_OK


def status(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    json.dump({r: get_rollout(r, args.flag) for r in args.regions} if args.flag else {}, sys.stdout, indent=2)
    print()
    return EXIT_OK

#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
# slo_burn.R -- nightly SLO burn-rate rollup for the GraphQL gateway and model serving
# owner: platform-sre (ping priya or tomas).  Runs in the `reports` CronJob, see deploy/k8s/reports.yaml
# NOTE: arrow::read_parquet segfaulted on the runner image, so the export job writes csv. Don't ask.

# fmt: markdown
# # SLO burn report
#
# This script is the **source of truth** for the availability and latency numbers in the weekly ops review. If the Grafana dashboard and this script disagree, the dashboard is wrong (it samples at 10%).
#
# Inputs:
# - `data/gateway_hourly_<region>_<date>.csv` from the `logs-export` job,
#     one file per region per day
# - `data/slo_targets.csv`, one row per (service, sli)
#
# A request is *good* if status < 500 and latency <= the per-operation threshold. Burn rate is (1 - SLI) / (1 - SLO), so 1.0 means we spend exactly the monthly budget.
#
# Known gaps:
#
# 1. ap-southeast-2 has no GPU nodes, so model-serving SLIs are `NA` there
# 2. requests rejected by the edge rate limiter never reach the gateway logs,
# so availability is slightly optimistic

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(data.table)
})

# fmt: markdown
usage <- "
Usage: Rscript slo_burn.R [data_dir] [out_dir]

Reads the hourly gateway exports from `data_dir` (default: data) and writes slo_burn.csv plus slo_burn.md into `out_dir` (default: out).
Set SLO_WINDOW_DAYS to change the 28 day window.
"

#| label: config
#| message:   false
#| warning: FALSE
#| params:
#|     window_days: 28
#|     regions: [us-east-1,eu-west-1,  ap-southeast-2]
#|     out_dir: "out/"
args <- commandArgs(trailingOnly = TRUE)
if (any(args %in% c("-h", "--help"))) { cat(usage); quit(status = 0) }
data_dir <- if (length(args) >= 1) args[[1]] else "data"
out_dir  <- if (length(args) >= 2) args[[2]] else "out"
window_days <- as.integer(Sys.getenv("SLO_WINDOW_DAYS", "28"))
regions <- c("us-east-1", "eu-west-1", "ap-southeast-2")
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# --- load --------------------------------------------------------------------
files <- list.files(data_dir, pattern = "^gateway_hourly_.*\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)
if (!length(files)) stop("no input files in ", data_dir, call. = FALSE)

# fill = TRUE because the export added `subgraph` in October and the old files don't have it
hourly <- rbindlist(lapply(files, fread, colClasses = list(character = c("region", "operation"))), fill = TRUE)
hourly[, hour := as.POSIXct(hour, format = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", tz = "UTC")]
hourly <- hourly[hour >= max(hour) - window_days * 86400 & region %in% regions]

targets <- fread(file.path(data_dir, "slo_targets.csv"))
setkey(targets, service, sli)

#| label: burn
#| cache:    true
#| dependson: ["config", 'load']
#| fig-cap: >
#|      Multi-window burn rate (1h / 6h) per region; the dashed line is the
#|      14.4x fast-burn page threshold from the SRE workbook.
#| fig-width: 9

---
title: "INC-2291 post-mortem: gateway brownout in eu-west-1"
subtitle:   Capacity review and follow-ups
author:
  - name: Priya Natarajan
    affiliation: Platform SRE
  - name: "Tomás Reyes"
    affiliation: ML Infra
date: 2024-10-21
date-modified: last-modified
description: Blameless post-mortem for the 47-minute partial outage of the public GraphQL gateway in eu-west-1 on 2024-10-17, plus the capacity model we now use to size the gateway and the ranker fleet for Q1.
format:
  html:
    toc: True
    toc-depth: 3
    toc-location: left
    code-fold: true
    code-summary: "Show the code"
    code-tools: true
    number-sections: true
    theme: [cosmo,  assets/postmortem.scss]
    fig-width: 8
    fig-height: 4
execute:
    echo: false
    warning: false
    freeze: auto
params:
  region: eu-west-1
  window_hours: 48
  slo_target: 0.999
---

{{< include _snippets/blameless-preamble.qmd >}}

::: {.callout-important}
## Summary
Between 14:02 and 14:49 UTC on 2024-10-17 roughly 18% of GraphQL requests in eu-west-1 failed or timed out. The trigger was a slow `accounts` subgraph (an index dropped by a migration); the reason it turned into a brownout rather than one slow field was that every router worker ended up waiting on that subgraph for up to 10 seconds.
:::

## Impact {#sec-impact}

- The 5xx ratio peaked at 23.4% (5-minute window) at 14:31, see @fig-errors.
- 47 minutes of SLO-relevant impact. The monthly error budget for the gateway (99.9%) was gone in that window
and then some.
- No data loss. Checkout retried client-side, so some users received duplicate "order received" emails[^dupes].
- Model serving was **not** affected directly, but ranker QPS dropped ~40% because fewer requests made it past the gateway.

## Timeline   { #sec-timeline   .unnumbered }

All times UTC on 2024-10-17. The raw version is in the incident doc; @tbl-timeline is the edited one.

| Time  | Event | Who |
|---|---|---|
| 13:55 | Migration `0142_accounts_drop_legacy_idx` applied in eu-west-1 by the deploy pipeline | pipeline |
| 14:02 | p99 of the `accounts` subgraph crosses 2s | - |
| 14:06 | `GatewayErrorBudgetFastBurn` fires (14.4x over 1h/5m) and pages the on-call | Alertmanager |
| 14:09 | On-call acks, starts looking at router dashboards | Priya |
| 14:12 | HPA starts adding router pods (CPU-based, so late) | HPA |
| 14:15 | Incident declared, IC assigned | Priya |
| 14:18 | First theory: flagd outage. Ruled out, flag eval p99 normal | Tomás |
| 14:21 | Router logs show `accounts` timeouts at exactly 10s | Priya |
| 14:24 | Tried to lower the subgraph timeout via hot reload; rejected because the ConfigMap was immutable | Priya |
| 14:27 | Rolled the router with a patched ConfigMap (`timeout: 2500ms`) | Priya |
| 14:31 | Peak: 23.4% 5xx. New pods fail readiness while warming the query planner cache | - |
| 14:34 | `accounts` team identifies the dropped index | accounts on-call |
| 14:38 | Index recreated with `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` | accounts on-call |
| 14:41 | `accounts` p99 back under 300ms | - |
| 14:44 | Router error ratio below 1% | - |
| 14:49 | Error ratio back to baseline, incident mitigated | IC |
| 15:30 | Revert of the migration merged so other regions don't repeat it | accounts team |
| 16:10 | Incident resolved | IC |

: Incident timeline (UTC) {#tbl-timeline}

## What happened {#sec-what-happened}

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-request-path
%%| fig-cap: "Request path during the incident. Thick edges were saturated."
flowchart LR
  C[Clients] --> NLB[NLB eu-west-1]
  NLB --> R[router pods x12]
  R ==>|10s timeout| A[(accounts subgraph)]
  R --> F[flagd]
  R --> M[ranker-v7 on Triton]
```

The router runs subgraph fetches concurrently, but each client request holds a worker until all of its fetches complete or time out. With a 10s timeout and ~3,900 rps in `{r} params$region`, a subgraph that suddenly takes 10s to answer ties up workers far faster than the HPA can add them (@fig-request-path).

```{r}
#| label: fig-errors
#| fig-cap: "5xx ratio in 5-minute windows. Dashed: 14.4x burn-rate threshold."
#| fig-width:   9
#| echo: FALSE
#| warning: no
library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)
err <- fread("data/inc2291_error_ratio.csv")
ggplot(err[region == params$region], aes(ts, ratio)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 14.4 * (1 - params$slo_target), linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent)
```

```{bash, label="replay-check", echo=TRUE, eval=FALSE, error=TRUE, class.source="bg-warning"}
# replay 10 minutes of production traffic against the patched config in staging
k6 run load/replay.js -e WINDOW=2024-10-17T14:20:00Z/PT10M -e TARGET=https://api.staging.kestrel.dev/graphql
```

## Capacity model {#sec-capacity}

We size router pods with Little's law. With peak arrival rate $\lambda$, mean time in system $W$, per-pod concurrency $c$ and a target utilisation $\rho$:

$$
N_{\text{pods}} = \left\lceil \frac{\lambda_{\text{peak}} \cdot W}{c \cdot \rho} \right\rceil
$$ {#eq-pods}

```{python}
#| label: tbl-capacity
#| tbl-cap: Router pods needed per region at Q1 peak (rho = 0.6)
#| echo:    true
#| code-fold: show
import math
peak_rps = {"us-east-1": 5200, "eu-west-1": 3900, "ap-southeast-2": 1400}
w_s, per_pod, rho = 0.180, 64, 0.6
print("| region | peak rps | pods |\n|---|---:|---:|")
for r, rps in peak_rps.items(): print(f"| {r} | {rps} | {math.ceil(rps * w_s / (per_pod * rho))} |")
```

::: {.panel-tabset}
## us-east-1
Headroom is fine. The current floor is 12 pods; @eq-pods gives 25 at Q1 peak, which the HPA reaches in under 2 minutes now that it also scales on in-flight requests.

## eu-west-1
This is the region that fell over. The floor goes from 6 to 12 pods permanently. With the 2.5s subgraph timeout the worst-case worker hold time drops by 4x, so the same incident would now cost roughly a quarter of the capacity.

## ap-southeast-2
Small region, but the ranker has no local GPU nodes and calls us-east-1 (~180ms extra).
That cross-region call counts against the router's time in system, which is why its pod count looks high for its traffic.
:::

```{r}
#| label: raw-dump
#| fmt: skip
#| eval:    false
x  <-  fread( "data/raw_router_logs.csv" )   # kept for reference, do not run
```

## Contributing factors

Brownout
:   A partial outage: the service is up, but a large share of requests fail or are too slow to be useful.

Burn rate
:     How fast the error budget is spent relative to the SLO window. A burn rate of 1 spends exactly the whole budget over 30 days; 14.4 spends 2% of it in one hour.

1. The default subgraph timeout (10s) was never tuned. It was copy-pasted from the router docs in 2023.
2. The HPA scaled on CPU only, and waiting workers don't use CPU[^hpa].
3. The router ConfigMap was marked `immutable: true`, so hot reload could not apply the fix and we had to roll pods during the incident -- which made it worse, because new pods start with a cold query-plan cache.

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="What went well"}
- The alert fired 4 minutes after the first errors.
- The flags team ruled out flagd in under 3 minutes thanks to the per-region flag eval dashboards.
::::

## Action items

---
title: "EXP-117: batched GraphQL queries on checkout -- A/B readout"
author: "Growth Eng x Platform SRE"
date: "`r format(Sys.Date(), '%d %B %Y')`"
output:
  html_document:
    toc: true
    toc_float: TRUE
    code_folding: hide
    df_print: paged
params:
    exp_id: "EXP-117"
    alpha: 0.05
    mde:   0.01
editor_options:
  markdown:
    wrap: sentence
    canonical: true
  chunk_output_type: console
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=4, dpi=150}
library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)
exp <- fread(here::here("data", "exp117_assignments.csv"))
n_control <- exp[arm == "control", uniqueN(user_id)]
n_treat <- exp[arm == "treatment", uniqueN(user_id)]
```

## TL;DR

We tested whether batching the three checkout queries (cart, shipping options, payment methods) into one persisted GraphQL operation reduces checkout abandonment. It does! Conversion in the treatment arm was 4.71% vs. 4.56% in control, a relative lift of 3.2%. The result is significant at the pre-registered alpha of `r params$alpha` (p = 0.012, two-sided) and the direction is the same in all three regions (see Sec. 4). We recommend shipping to 100% behind the existing flag `checkout.batched-queries` and deleting the flag after two weeks.

## Background

Checkout makes three round-trips to the gateway before the "Pay" button becomes active. On mobile networks in ap-southeast-2 that is approx. 900 ms of extra latency at the median and roughly 2.1 s at the p90. Product had a hunch that this mattered; the platform team had a hunch that it didn't, i.e. that users wait anyway. One reviewer called the whole thing "premature optimization." This experiment was meant to settle the question (and, frankly, the argument).

The design follows the usual playbook (cf. the experimentation guide, p. 4): user-level randomization via flagd's `fractional` operator, a 50/50 split, and a fixed horizon of 14 days from a power analysis for an MDE of `r scales::percent(params$mde)` relative.
Dr. Okafor reviewed the analysis plan before launch on Oct. 2. We did not peek... well, we peeked once, on day 3, because the dashboard was public. We did _not_ act on it.

## Data

```{r load}
#| echo:    false
#| cache: TRUE
#| dependson: [ "setup" ]
orders <- fread(here::here("data", "exp117_orders.csv"))
conv <- merge(exp, orders[, .(converted = any(status == "created")), by = user_id], by = "user_id", all.x = TRUE)
conv[is.na(converted), converted := FALSE]
```

Assignment was balanced: `r format(n_control, big.mark = ",")` users in control vs. `r format(n_treat, big.mark = ",")` in treatment (SRM check p = 0.41). Bots, internal users (e.g. anyone with a `kestrel.dev` address) and users who never reached the cart were excluded before assignment, not after. About 0.8% of sessions were dropped because old app versions (< 5.12) ignore the flag and keep sending the unbatched operations. These users were in both arms in equal numbers, so this shouldn't bias anything.

## Results

### Primary metric: checkout conversion

```{r primary, fig.cap="Conversion by arm with 95% CI."}
res <- conv[, .(rate = mean(converted), n = .N), by = arm]
res[, se := sqrt(rate * (1 - rate) / n)]
ggplot(res, aes(arm, rate)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = rate - 1.96 * se, ymax = rate + 1.96 * se)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent)
```

Treatment converted at 4.71% and control at 4.56%. The absolute difference is 0.15 percentage points (95% CI: 0.03 to 0.27). That is a relative lift of 3.2%. Is that a lot? For checkout, yes: at current volume it is worth roughly $41k per month in recovered orders, give or take novelty effects, seasonality, etc. The U.S. holiday season starts in four weeks, so the real number may well be higher.

### Secondary metrics

- __Time to interactive on the payment step__ dropped from 1.84 s to 1.12 s at the median. The p90 improved even more (3.9 s to 2.2 s), mostly in ap-southeast-2.
- __Gateway load.__ Batching cut checkout-related requests by 61%. CPU per request went up a bit because the batched operation is larger, but total checkout CPU fell by approx. 35%.
- __Error rate__ was flat at 0.21% in both arms. We were worried that one failing subgraph would now fail the whole batch. It didn't, because the router returns partial data plus an `errors` array instead of failing the operation (see Fig. 2 in the gateway docs).

### By region

```{r by-region}
#| tbl-cap:   "Relative lift by region with 95% CI"
#| echo: false
by_region <- conv[, .(rate = mean(converted)), by = .(region, arm)]
knitr::kable(dcast(by_region, region ~ arm, value.var = "rate"), digits = 4)
```

The effect is largest in ap-southeast-2 (+5.9%), where round-trips are slowest, and smallest in us-east-1 (+2.4%). That matches the latency story nicely! Note that the per-region intervals are wide; with n = 14,180 per arm in ap-southeast-2 we can't claim the regions differ from each other (interaction p = 0.18).

| Region | Control | Treatment | Lift |
|---|---|---|---|
| us-east-1 | 4.61% | 4.72% | +2.4% |
| eu-west-1 | 4.55% | 4.69% | +3.1% |
| ap-southeast-2 | 4.38% | 4.64% | +5.9% |

## Caveats

1. The experiment overlapped with INC-2291. We excluded the 47 minutes of the eu-west-1 brownout (14:02 to 14:49 UTC on Oct. 17). Including them moves the lift to 3.0%, so the conclusion holds.
2. "Conversion" means an order was created, not that it was paid. Payment failures are tracked separately and were flat (0.9% in both arms).
3. Novelty effects are unlikely for a pure latency change. We'll keep a 5% holdout for another month anyway!

## Recommendation

Ship it. Ramp `checkout.batched-queries` to 100% in all regions with `rollout.py ramp` (steps 50 and 100), keep the 5% holdout until Dec. 1, then delete the flag[^cleanup]. Questions? Ask in the growth-eng channel or ping the authors directly.

[^cleanup]: The flags-janitor bot opens the removal PR by itself once the flag passes its `expires` date. Please merge it rather than bumping the date.

    81	    - propagate: {matching: "^x-kestrel-.*"}
    82	include_subgraph_errors: { all: true }
    83	```
    84	
    85	Restart with <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>C</kbd> and `make dev` again; hot reload only watches `router.yaml`, not the supergraph.  
    86	
    87	## Feature flags
    88	
    89	Flags live in `flags/flags.yaml` and are served by [flagd] in every region. The workflow:
    90	
    91	1. Edit `flags/flags.yaml` (or use `tools/rollout/rollout.py`)
    92	   - flag keys are `<service>.<feature>` in kebab-case
    93	   - every flag needs an `owner` and an `expires` date, CI fails otherwise
    94	2. Open a PR. The `flags-lint` job evaluates the JsonLogic rules against a sample context and
    95	posts a diff of the evaluated variants for ~2k synthetic users.
    96	3. After merge flagd picks up the change within ~30s
    97	    * staging first, then the canary region, then the rest
    98	    * need it faster? `kubectl -n flags rollout restart deploy/flagd` -- but not during business hours please
    99	
   100	<!-- fmt: off -->
   101	| Region         | Gateway p99 | Flag eval p99 |
   102	|----------------|------------:|--------------:|
   103	| us-east-1      |      182 ms |        1.9 ms |
   104	| eu-west-1      |      240 ms |        2.4 ms |
   105	| ap-southeast-2 |      311 ms |        3.1 ms |
   106	
   107	*   numbers from the October load test,
   108	    pasted into the quarterly deck as-is,
   109	    please don't reformat
   110	<!-- fmt: on -->
   111	
   112	##   Runbooks ##
   113	
   114	- [Gateway: restart / drain](docs/runbooks/gateway/restart.md)
   115	- [Gateway: subgraph timeouts](<docs/runbooks/gateway/subgraph timeouts.md>)
   116	- [Flags: flagd returns defaults everywhere](docs/runbooks/flags.md#everything-is-default "the scary one")
   117	- [GPU nodes stuck `NotReady`](docs/runbooks/gpu-notready.md)
   118	
   119	The gateway enforces persisted queries in production[^apq] and a per-operation cost limit[^cost]. If you
   120	see `PERSISTED_QUERY_NOT_IN_LIST` in staging, that is a client bug, not ours. Ask the client team to
   121	re-run `pq-publish` for their release before you open an incident.
   122	
   123	<details>
   124	<summary>Why no service mesh for the gateway?</summary>
   125	
   126	We tried Istio in 2023. Short version: an extra hop, ~4ms of p50, and a sidecar that OOMed under the query-planner warmup. Details in [ADR-009](docs/adr/009-no-mesh-for-gateway.md).
   127	
   128	</details>
   129	
   130	## Roadmap (Q4)
   131	   
   132	- [x] Persisted queries enforced on the public gateway
   133	- [x] KServe 0.13 upgrade   
   134	- [ ] Delete the LaunchDarkly sync job :skull:
   135	- [ ] ap-southeast-2 GPU pool
   136	  - [ ] quota request for `g5` instances
   137	  - [X] Triton model warmup on scale-up
   138	- [ ] Active-active writes for the flags DB (needs an ADR first)
   139	
   140	
   141	
   142	Contributing
   143	------------
   144	
   145	Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) first. TL;DR: small PRs, a ticket number in the title, and never `kubectl edit` in prod without writing it down in the incident channel.
   146	More background reading: the [Apollo Router docs][router], [flagd][], and the [KServe docs][kserve] (we use `RawDeployment` mode, so ignore everything about Knative).
   147	
   148	[router]: https://www.apollographql.com/docs/router/ "Apollo Router"
   149	[flagd]: https://flagd.dev/
   150	[kserve]: <https://kserve.github.io/website/latest/> 'KServe documentation'
   151	
   152	[^apq]: Automatic persisted queries are still allowed in staging so that Apollo Studio Explorer keeps working. In prod the router rejects unknown hashes.
   153	[^cost]: Cost is estimated from the static query plan, not measured at runtime. See `services/gateway/plugins/cost_limit.rs` if you want to argue about the weights.

     2	title:   "Contributing to kestrel/platform"
     3	description: How we review, test and ship changes to the platform monorepo (infra, the GraphQL gateway, feature flags and model serving). Read this before your first PR, it will save you a round of review.

    12	
    13	# Contributing   
    14	
    15	Thanks for helping keep the platform upright! :wave: This page covers the boring-but-important parts: how to set up, how we name things, what a reviewable PR looks like and how releases go out. It is opinionated because almost every rule here exists because of a specific incident.
    16	
    17	## Ground rules
    18	
    19	- **Small PRs.** Under ~400 changed lines unless it is generated code. Big refactors get split or get an ADR
    20	first.
    21	- Every PR title starts with a ticket: `PLAT-1234: ...`. Hotfixes during an incident can use the incident id instead (`INC-2291: ...`).
    22	- Don't `kubectl apply` or `kubectl edit` against prod from your laptop. If you absolutely have to (you are the IC, the pipeline is down, etc.) write down every command in the incident channel *as you run it*.
    23	-   Feature flags are not a substitute for a rollback plan.  
    24	
    25	## Local setup
    26	
    27	1. Install the toolchain:
    28	   ```console
    29	   $ brew bundle --file=Brewfile
    30	   $ uv tool install pre-commit && pre-commit install --install-hooks
    31	   ```
    32	2. Log in to AWS SSO (`aws sso login --profile kestrel-dev`) and run `make bootstrap`.
    33	3) Run `make dev` and check that <http://localhost:4000> serves the sandbox.
    34	
    35	Pre-commit runs `ruff`, `yamllint`, `helm lint`, `shellcheck` and `yamark format --check`. If a hook rewrites files, just `git add` them and commit again -- that is not a failure.
    36	
    37	
    38	## Commits and branches
    39	
    40	We use [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/) because the changelog generator depends on it.
    60	
    61	Copy this into the PR description if the template didn't load:
    62	
    63	- [ ] Ticket id in the title
    64	- [ ] `make test` passes locally
    65	- [ ] Dashboards / alerts updated if you renamed a metric
    66	- [ ] New flags have an `owner` and an `expires` date
    67	- [x] I read this document :)
    68	
    69	## Feature flags
    70	
    71	> Flags are config, not code. Treat a flag flip like a deploy.
    72	>
    73	> ```yaml
    74	> gateway.query-planner-v2:
    75	>     state: ENABLED
    76	>     owner: gateway-team
    77	>     expires: 2025-01-31
    78	>     variants: {on: true,off: false}
    79	>     defaultVariant: off
    80	> ```
    81	
    82	Flags are cheap to add and expensive to keep around.
    83	Every stale flag is a branch in the code that nobody
    84	tests anymore, and an extra evaluation on the hot path
    85	of the gateway. Some rules that came out of the last
    86	two quarters of incidents:
    87	
    88	* Name flags `<service>.<feature>`, lowercase, kebab-case after the dot.
    89	* Default to `off`. A flag that defaults to `on` is a deploy in disguise
    90	  and has to go through the normal release review.
    91	* Remove flags within two sprints of reaching 100%. The `flags-janitor` bot opens a PR for every flag past its `expires` date; please don't just bump the date.
    92	
    93	## Tests 
    94	
    95	```console
    96	$ make test                       # unit tests, ~2 min
    97	$ pytest tools/rollout -k "ramp and not slow" -q
    98	$ k6 run load/gateway-smoke.js --vus 20 --duration 60s
    99	```

    31	## TL;DR
    32	
    33	We tested whether batching the three checkout queries (cart, shipping options, payment methods) into one persisted GraphQL operation reduces checkout abandonment. It does! Conversion in the treatment arm was 4.71% vs. 4.56% in control, a relative lift of 3.2%. The result is significant at the pre-registered alpha of `r params$alpha` (p = 0.012, two-sided) and the direction is the same in all three regions (see Sec. 4). We recommend shipping to 100% behind the existing flag `checkout.batched-queries` and deleting the flag after two weeks.
    34	
    35	## Background 
    36	
    37	Checkout makes three round-trips to the gateway before the "Pay" button becomes active. On mobile networks in ap-southeast-2 that is approx. 900 ms of extra latency at the median and roughly 2.1 s at the p90. Product had a hunch that this mattered; the platform team had a hunch that it didn't, i.e. that users wait anyway. One reviewer called the whole thing "premature optimization." This experiment was meant to settle the question (and, frankly, the argument).
    38	
    39	The design follows the usual playbook (cf. the experimentation guide, p. 4): user-level randomization via flagd's `fractional` operator, a 50/50 split, and a fixed horizon of 14 days from a power analysis for an MDE of `r scales::percent(params$mde)` relative.
    40	Dr. Okafor reviewed the analysis plan before launch on Oct. 2. We did not peek... well, we peeked once, on day 3, because the dashboard was public. We did _not_ act on it.  
    41	
    42	## Data
    43	
    44	```{r load}
    45	#| echo:    false
...
    30	  window_hours: 48
    31	  slo_target: 0.999
    32	---
    33	
    34	{{< include _snippets/blameless-preamble.qmd >}}
    35	
    36	
    37	::: {.callout-important}
    38	## Summary
    39	Between 14:02 and 14:49 UTC on 2024-10-17 roughly 18% of GraphQL requests in eu-west-1 failed or timed out. The trigger was a slow `accounts` subgraph (an index dropped by a migration); the reason it turned into a brownout rather than one slow field was that every router worker ended up waiting on that subgraph for up to 10 seconds.
    40	:::
    41	
    42	## Impact {#sec-impact}  
    43	
    44	- The 5xx ratio peaked at 23.4% (5-minute window) at 14:31, see @fig-errors.
    45	- 47 minutes of SLO-relevant impact. The monthly error budget for the gateway (99.9%) was gone in that window
   150	
   151	
   152	
   153	## Contributing factors
   154	
   155	Brownout
   156	:   A partial outage: the service is up, but a large share of requests fail or are too slow to be useful.
   157	
   158	Burn rate
   159	:     How fast the error budget is spent relative to the SLO window. A burn rate of 1 spends exactly the whole budget over 30 days; 14.4 spends 2% of it in one hour.
   160	
   161	1. The default subgraph timeout (10s) was never tuned. It was copy-pasted from the router docs in 2023.
   162	2. The HPA scaled on CPU only, and waiting workers don't use CPU[^hpa].
   163	3. The router ConfigMap was marked `immutable: true`, so hot reload could not apply the fix and we had to roll pods during the incident -- which made it worse, because new pods start with a cold query-plan cache.
